Settle the treatment in conversation, then write out/visual-treatment.json (one entry per gap: gap_id, the team's intended visuals cited or departed from with the reason, the picture in one line, the route, the seconds, for a video gap its segments with their seconds, the images it needs (segments plus one for video); then the counts per route, the seconds of graphics and the estimated cost against the cap) then `vw visuals treatment --file out/visual-treatment.json` sends it to the visuals page as the draft, where the operator reads it gap by gap and approves it with their words; in chat instead, present it and on their yes run the same command with --quote "<their yes>". Nothing else before this: no plan, no image. For every graphic, list what it depicts (`depicts`), and for every gap its `activity_level` (quiet, normal or busy). Give each entry `frozen_seconds`, the seconds of the gap held without movement (usually 0); the treatment shows the film's frozen share against its 10 % limit. The first gap opens on the strongest picture of the film's subject, not a neutral establishing shot. When a gap has no real footage beside it, propose its look in the treatment: the palette, the contrast, the saturation (muted and true to life by default) and the light; the operator approves it with the treatment.

Author out/visual-plan.json to the recorded treatment (foundation, elements, gaps with scenes, shots, states for every animation shot, beats). Give every scene with a video shot its ambient line: one line saying what moves around the action (leaves and fronds in the breeze, dust or smoke in the air, people in the background at work), chosen from the setting and the footage beside the gap, or 'still' when nothing else should move; the server writes it into every take and the take check asks for it. `vw visuals check --file out/visual-plan.json` until valid; it prints the routes, the graphic seconds, the images and the cost against the cap; answer every warning in the shot's purpose and show them to the operator. `vw visuals propose --file …` (refused until the treatment is recorded or when a route departs from it); `vw visuals select --gap G --choice C` where offered; `vw visuals accept --gaps all --quote "…"` (or the gaps they named). Then read every gap's words in `vw visuals status` before any picture. A gap under revision (Revise on the page, or `vw visuals revise --gap G --notes "…" --quote "…"` on the operator's words) and accepted words that ask for a change are a revision of that gap: change its treatment entry and plan, propose the next version, and it is accepted afresh; generate nothing for it until then. Timing, movement and no repeats. Each gap carries its narration timed (gaps.json `timing`: sentences in seconds, words in frames; the packet's context.timing adds the sentences on either side). Cut in a pause between sentences or phrases, never inside a word; a shot's `narration` is the words it covers, and its picture starts on or just before them; a title or label starts on its word. Every still and graphic state moves 5 %: set `motion` from the composition (push_in, push_out, pan_left, pan_right; graphics push_in only); `none` needs `motion_reason`. A moving still runs at most 4 s, a frozen one 3 s; a graphic state at most 5 s; a graphic over 4 s is a build of 2 to 4 states. Fill a longer stretch with several stills, a clip stretch (`vw visuals clip --shot S --clip C --at <in seconds>`) or a take. The film never shows one picture twice: a clip already on screen, in the first cut or here, is a reuse, and a frozen frame of a clip that plays elsewhere is never shown. When the narration returns to a subject, plan a reimagined shot: `return_of` the earlier shot and `differs_by` (the angle, distance or moment), the earlier picture only as an identity reference. A plain reuse only when the reimagined shot adds nothing: `vw visuals clip|still … --reuse "<reason>" --considered "<the reimagined shot and why it adds nothing>" --crop x,y,w,h`, at least 60 s from the other showing, a different stretch, a crop within the clip's safe enlargement; it then waits for the operator's own words (on the page, or `vw visuals reuse --shot S --quote "<their words>"`). Two shots never share a start image or a still. The check warns on cuts off a pause, pictures off their words, long stills, the frozen share and pictures that look alike: answer each in the shot's purpose or change the plan. Graphics: every graphic shot lists its `claims`, or names one left out in `claims_left_out` with the reason; every state of a build names its `words`; foundation.graphic_style once. A drawing of a real object carries a `drawing_spec`: its parts, its relationships, each size with its status (confirmed, measured, unknown) and its source; an unknown size has no value, is never invented, and the label says "illustrative, not to scale". Measure from approved footage frames: `vw visuals measure --refs F1 F2 --question "<what to measure>"` (each number keeps its clip and time). Sources in this order: the client's own material; the footage, measured; a standard or a manufacturer's sheet on the web, on the operator's yes, with its URL and figure; an approved reference picture for a shape numbers cannot hold. Show the operator the spec as a table and record their words: `vw visuals spec --shot S --quote "…"` (or on the page). Make the style sheet first, `image --element _STYLE --kind style --answer …`, approve it and name it in every graphic's --parents; every picture and every take carries its --answer. Missing claims, style, spec approval or answer forms are warned in this release and refused from the next. Change list and action budget: every video shot lists its `changes` (what differs between its start and end picture, and the `beat_id` of the beat that causes it), and every beat its `min_s` (the realistic time its action takes); the check refuses a beat shorter than its action and a subject whose actions need more than the shot's seconds. Scenes that make sense: every shot lists its `claims` and `descriptors` and, when it carries a claim, its `evidence`; `visual_facts` (looks, how, setting, tools, with source and status confirmed, observed or unknown) for every material, process and setting shown, named by `fact_ids`; an unknown fact is never invented (a close shot on it is refused); every graphic its `depicts` and its `graphic_kind` (diagram, chart, map, title, text; a step of a build is checked for what it shows); the next step of a process its `carries_over`. Life, intent, one world, one message: every scene its `activity_level` and, when normal or busy, background subjects with beats; every moving subject's target in frame at the start or it comes into view; the foundation's `studio_background` only when the treatment allows a plain background; every shot its `message`, and `adds` when it repeats one. Builds, labels, frame and joins: a build has a state per claim; labels are short phrases with units, at least 4 % of the frame height (titles 6 %), in the answer's exact text; a clip that cannot fill the frame within 1.35× gets a crop or another clip; transitions default to an 8-frame dissolve at graphics and a cut elsewhere, and a chosen `transition_in` or `transition_out` carries its `transition_reason`. Props by context: show what is normal for the work and the region (a tea glass on a site), never what the setting forbids (no smoking, flame or spark near fuel, gas or chemicals), and no unsafe practice shown as the right way. Work leaves traces: tools, offcuts, mortar droppings, footprints on an active site; signs of use in a finished house; never staged empty unless the treatment says so. Give each scene its light once (light: the sources against the landmarks, the main one, hard or soft, colour, strength) and its air (dust, smoke, haze, steam, or clean; matched to the footage), each shot its size (EWS, WS, MWS, MS, MCU, CU, ECU: a new place opens wide, a close-up comes after the subject is seen wider, a reveal is stated in size_reason) and its camera_reason (what the viewer should feel or read, and why this angle, size and move give it: eye level is honest, low is powerful, high is vulnerable, a slow push draws in, handheld feels raw; no angle has one fixed meaning), and a claim its kind (visible: a camera could film it, so footage first; invisible: a graphic may show it). When footage shows a person speaking to camera, offer non-speaking angles of them (listening, hands at work, profile, from behind), footage first, AI only where none exists. Before a drawing spec is shown, research it: fill every size it depends on from the sources, in order: the client's material; `vw visuals measure` on footage frames (paid: announce it, never ask); a standard or a maker figure from the web (one warning and yes covers every spec of the run); an approved reference picture. Each value carries its source and status. A spec of a real object always carries its proportions (the ratios that matter, for example a brick about 3 : 1.5 : 1); "illustrative" means no numbers printed, never free proportions. A size is `unknown` only after the sources were tried, recorded in `tried` with why each failed. The operator is never asked to type a size: they approve every spec of the run in one table (`vw visuals spec` with no --shot, or the page), or send a correction (`vw visuals spec --shot S --notes "…"`; it shows under `spec_corrections` in `vw visuals status`), which you fold into the plan with `planning revise` before they approve; an approval is refused while a correction waits.

The references are one round, every element at once, never one element at a time: `vw visuals elements` (where each is seen in the footage, work/visuals/elements.json); grab a frame for every element the footage has (`frame --file`) (`frame`, free); write out/reference-round.json, one row per person, object or place: element_id, its frame reference ids, the two-to-six-word keywords you would search; `vw visuals round --file out/reference-round.json`; give the operator the page link once; `vw visuals status --wait 900` until the round is complete (on pass 1 the operator answers every thing: use the footage picture, Search (each thing's own button: the plain search and, with the source word, a stock search beside it, every picture downloaded at once), or Ignore this; Done waits until every thing set to Google is searched. On pass 2 every searched thing gets a tick with notes, new words and Search again, or Ignore this; Done waits for all of them); ask nothing per element and generate nothing meanwhile. Use the wait, for accepted gaps only, a gap under revision skipped: write, without generating or spending, the answer forms of every diagram, chart and title card, the drawing specs and the material specs from the client's own material and the plan (a paid measure or a web figure waits for after the round), and the drawn layouts as drafts on your side; nothing new on the operator's page and no question while the round is open; questions the drafts raise are asked after the round as one list; update a draft the round changed (an element ignored) before using it. One round is the default, but at any time the operator can redo one element on the page (Search again, Nothing fits stay on every card, also after Done and after the sheet), add their own picture (Add your own picture on the page, or `vw visuals supply`), or undo Done until the next step used it (`vw visuals round --undo`: pass 1 until a pick is saved, pass 2 until a sheet was made); redoing one element never touches the others; a picture added after the sheet marks that sheet 'sources changed' (status, waiting, the card): make a new sheet, the old one stays approved until the new one is. Then one sheet per element from its approved frames and picks (`image --kind sheet --parents F1,W2`, the notes added by the server under their pictures) and tell the operator the sheets are on the page to approve. The single calls below serve an operator who answers in chat: `search --element E --keywords "…" --source <site> --quote "…"` for each thing they send to Google, then `round --verdicts out/round-verdicts.json --quote` ({element: {verdict: approve|search|ignore}}), then `round --picks out/round-picks.json --quote` ({search id: [{n, note}], "ignore": [elements]}). Materials and processes the film relies on (kind material or process) are elements in the round like people, objects and places. A start keyframe or a picture for a still names its shot (`--shot S`, or `shot` per row in the file) so its claims, words, the state carried over and its facts are checked. References per element, in this order: a frame from a clip (`vw visuals frame --element E --clip <id> --at <s>`, free), the operator's file (`supply`), for what the footage lacks, Google Images on their yes (`search --element E --keywords "<two to six words: the thing and its place or trade>" --source <stock site, outside the six words; empty for the plain search alone> --quote "<their yes>"`; with a source two searches come back, the plain one and the stock one; the ten pictures go to the visuals page, the operator ticks and notes them, or tells you: `pick --search S --n 2,5 --note 2="…" --quote "…"`; the picked pictures are approved when saved: show them, and reject one only if the saved file is not the picture ticked; a "nothing fits" reason joins the element's not-this list, and the next search is the operator's own words (or Ignore this), never yours; `nothing-fits --search S --reason "…"` in chat), a generated image (a start keyframe for a video shot only after that shot's `bind` and `packet`; `image --file out/images.json` for several at once, or `image --element E --kind keyframe --prompt "…"`, each with `--answer out/answers/<id>.json`, the library's answer form, or an `answer` path per item in the file; paid OpenAI GPT Image 2.5; inform, do not ask; the server refuses a call that would pass the cap). For a diagram, chart or labelled picture write every label and number in the prompt exactly and check each on the candidate before asking for approval. A state of a sequence: `image --element E --kind state --parents <previous state> --prompt "<only what changes>"`. The end image of a video shot: `image --element E --kind keyframe --parents <start keyframe> --prompt "<only what changes>"`, as soon as the start candidate exists; show the pair together and approve both. After a drift or a rejection, make the next end image from the approved start, never from a candidate; a state from the last approved state. A frame that shows a face is a look reference only, never a parent. After submitting a wave of images, write the next shot's answers (and its end image from the start candidate at once: one approval wave per shot) instead of waiting; `vw visuals status --wait 300` only when nothing is left to write. Show each candidate (`fetch --ref R`) and record their yes: `approve --ref R --sha <sha> --quote "…"`, several at once with `approve --file out/approvals.json` (rows of ref, sha, quote), or on the page. Then one sheet per person, object or place: `image --element E --kind sheet --parents F1,W2` from its frames and picks, the notes added by the server under their pictures, a person as posture, dress, build and features only (a frame or a pick of a person is never a parent for an edit); the sheet is what shots bind. An edit names each picture it sends as Image 1 to Image N, with what to take from it. A failed check marks the picture and shows its lines; a fix is made only on request: `vw visuals fix --ref R` (paid: tell the operator the line and the cost), or Try a fix on the page. When anything waits for the operator, give them the label and the link that `vw visuals status` prints for it (for example "Still · B01_S2" and its link), never only "on the page"; after each verdict, tell them the line the server answers with (what happens next, with the film time). On the visuals page a verdict is one click with no typed words: approve, Use for the shot, Remove, select a take, search, save the ticked pictures, the round's Done; a Reject's reason is optional (quick chips or a short note). In chat pass the operator's words as `--quote` when they give some. Grab the sharpest frame, the subject large and evenly lit; never a blurred frame as an identity source. Two people in one film wear clothes of different colour families, unless the footage fixes their clothes. Give every person, object, animal and material its real size (size: height, width, depth or length, each with its source and status), from the client's material, `measure` on footage frames, or a maker's sheet; unknown when none, never invented. Every repeating material (kind material, or `repeating: true`: bricks, tiles, blocks, planks, pavers) carries one `material_spec` on the element (unit sizes with sources, `laid`, `joint`, `pattern`, `proportions`), made like a drawing spec from the same sources and never typed by the operator; it is shown on the References step beside the sheet and approved once (`vw visuals spec --element E`, or the page; a correction: `vw visuals spec --element E --notes`); the server pastes its sentence into every prompt that shows the material and checks the unit ratio and the pattern as a must line; no picture of the material is made before the approval; relative words (short, long, about 2:1, roughly, standard) are refused in your prompt. Every element's 'not this' list is the server's: `vw visuals not-this --element E` builds it once from the round's near misses, one model call on the spec and this film's rejections (a material's is built with its spec approval when missing; every later rejection adds its words); the server pastes it into every prompt that shows the element; a shot that needs an exception names it in `allows` and the line says so. The golden picture: as soon as an element's sheet (and its material spec) is approved, `status.golden_due` names it: write its golden picture at once, no question to the operator (`vw visuals image --element E --kind isolated --golden --parents <sheet>,<footage frame> --prompt`: the element in its real place at the shot size the plan uses most; a client's own object sends its footage frame here and never again); the operator approves it beside the sheet; a person's identity sheet is its golden picture. Every later picture of the element has the golden picture as Image 1 ("Image 1 is the [element]. Repeat it exactly; change nothing about it. The only change is: …"); a derived picture is never a parent (an end is made from its approved start; a graphic's states chain); a fix round's output is never a parent; a picture approved with a stated flaw cannot be golden. Every end image is an edit inside one region of its start (several places or the framing itself: a start-only take instead): `--region left,top,width,height` (or `--end-region` with the start, for the end the server queues; fractions of the frame, a third at most; name the landmark in the prompt); the server masks it and copies the start back outside it; an end where several things change, or the framing, is made whole as before. Words to be read in a picture (a title, a label, a sign, a word on a bag) go only through the answer's `exact_text`, each entry {text, place: {landmark_id} or {region: 'lower third, inside the safe area'}, size_pct}; an entry with no place or size is refused, quoted words in the prompt that are not an entry are refused, and the server writes 'Render exactly this text, letter for letter, nothing else: …' and checks reads-exactly, the place and no other lettering on every picture. Up to sixteen pictures go in with a prompt (the model's limit), in this order: the picture edited or the scene parent, one identity sheet per person in frame, then every approved frame, golden picture or supplied reference of a thing in the shot (its tool, its material, its look); each with one job line ('Image k is …: take …, nothing else'); a picture goes in only when its thing is in the shot's element_ids (the style, a person in frame and the start excepted; the server refuses the rest by name); a parent may be cropped to the thing with `--parents K1,L2@left,top,width,height` (fractions of the frame; the server crops before the upload, stores the crop beside the picture and the check reads the crop); the server adds to every prompt the known sizes of the shot's elements as numbers ('Sizes: Broom: broom length 600 mm'), the height words of the layout ('Heights: the plinth top reaches a standing person's knee …') and, for a picture of another thing sent for its look, what that picture also shows ('Image k also shows a bicycle and a clay pot: show none of them'), each such thing a must line of the check. Once an element's sources are approved the server cues its reference sheet like the golden picture (`sheet_due` in status): write it at once with every source as a parent; the server adds the required views, each labelled, and 'the thing alone on plain ground'. A thing whose fact or size cites the footage is `identity: exact` and has an approved footage frame before any picture of it (the plan warns, the server refuses); a thing with a frame and a size still unknown is measured first (`vw visuals measure`) and the value put in the plan as measured. A background person who only passes is never a named element with a sheet: the scene says them in words, different in every scene. For each exact object, make a scale reference: a footage frame with a hand or a person beside it; else an edit placing it beside two or three objects of the same shoot at true relative size, with no text. When a shot shows a client material at medium or closer, bind its footage frame as the texture reference; in a place with a footage frame, bind that frame as the look reference (the packet's bind_advice names them).

Still shots need no bind or packet: approving the picture made for the shot places it (approving places it; `vw visuals unplace --shot S --quote "…"` takes it out); `still --shot S --ref R --quote "…"` places a footage frame or a picture approved before, or several in one call `still --file out/stills.json` (rows of shot, ref, quote). Video shots first: `bind --shot S --refs E1=R1,R2 E2=R3` (no quote: the approved references are the yes; several at once `bind --file out/bindings.json`, rows of shot, refs, selectors), then `packet --shot S`, then the start image, then the end image from the start candidate at once, the pair shown together; never a start image before the packet (the server refuses it). Animation shots: `sequence --shot S --quote "…"`, the states in the order they were made, shown together first. Video shots: `generator --shot S --provider … --model …` only when the shot is longer than the default makes (the check warns); `prepare-take --shot S --start R --end R2 --motion "…" --subject E1="…" --answer out/answers/<id>.json` for each (the end only for a shot with `end_state_exact`; the next segment's `--start` is this `--end`; when an end is sent, the server measures the pair's alignment in code and refuses a shifted or zoomed end with the figure, the motion text always states the camera, locked off on a tripod unless the shot's `camera_move` names its one move, every retained take is measured for drift in code, and a locked-off take whose frame drifts or zooms over 2 % fails the must line 'camera drift' with the figure on its card). A shot under 4 s with no visible action is a moving still by default (a footage frame or an AI still with a push or a pan); AI video or a graphic build there needs its reason in `purpose` ('because …'), the check warns without one; a still that carries words (`carries_text`, every graphic, a picture with exact text) moves by push_in or not at all and is placed whole, never cropped or panned (the renderer refuses a pan on it); the route counts show moving and frozen stills apart. A graphic with measurements, quantities, sequences or labels that must be exact takes the drawn route: `visual_type: drawn` with `scene_svg`; the scene is one SVG file (data, never code), uploaded first with `vw visuals scene --shot S --file scene.svg` and named in the plan by the sha256 the upload returns, with `actions` (appear, build, move, highlight, fade; `ids` are element ids of the SVG; a `build` on a `<g>` steps through its children `every_s` apart) keyed to `at_s` or a `word` of the shot's narration; the SVG keeps to a viewBox of the film's aspect (16:9), plain shapes, paths, text, g, use, gradients, filters, clipPath and mask, #RRGGBB colours from the approved palette, the fonts Noto Sans or the run's brand font, every text at least 4 % of the frame height, at most eight words and inside the inner 90 % of the frame, no script, no style element, no animation, no external link; the things in it are pictures: `<image href="ref:<id>">` of an approved component or the golden picture (a thing is never drawn from shapes when a picture can show it), and the drawn layer adds the exact parts (labels with their units, arrows, bars, courses as `<use>` repeats); a drawing spec is required when the shot carries figures, its known sizes are written as labels with their units and an unknown size shows no figure; `vw visuals draw --shot S` renders it free: the server checks the rules, measures every text, renders in Chromium, reads a contact sheet of every frame against the shot's lines with the style and the shot's pictures, corrects the SVG and renders again up to twice, then shows the drawing, its sheet and what it fixed on the Takes step; a drawing whose must lines still fail is held: `select` needs `--notes` saying why it is taken, else reject it with what to change; `vw visuals scene --shot S --download` brings the server's corrected SVG back; the film's brand font is given once with `vw visuals font --file brand.ttf`, Noto Sans otherwise. A component is the picture of one thing a drawn shot places: `vw visuals image --element E --kind component --prompt "one <thing>, front on"`, made in the approved style (the style picture is Image 1, added by the server) on a transparent background, checked for one thing alone with a clean edge and a transparent PNG, approved on the Pictures step like any picture, then reused by every scene of the run. The drawn route is for what must be exact: sizes, counts, a sequence of courses, a comparison of measured things; a diagram or build with exact sizes or numbers that is not drawn is refused; a conceptual graphic with nothing exact (an idea, icons, a mood) is a picture, a still with a push-in or a graphic sequence of states, never shapes standing for things; the usual drawn shot is the hybrid: the approved pictures placed as images, the exact parts drawn over them; AI video for graphics stays off; read the reply of each `prepare-take`: a difference between the pictures with no cause in the change list is marked (on the Takes step too); show it to the operator, who approves the pair or has the end image changed; then `take --shots all` (paid; inform) and `status --wait 600` until every take is ready (one line per job; whole in work/visuals/status.json); each ready take is read by Gemini first (about ₹1–2 a take, informed): its marks are in the status line and on the take's card; tell the operator what was marked, then `fetch --job J`, let the operator watch, and on their yes `select --job J --notes "<what you checked>" --quote "…"`; on a no `review --job J --decision rejected --notes "…" --quote "…"` and prepare again only when they ask for a correction. A file the operator supplies, on their instruction only: `vw upload --stage visuals --file out/x.mp4` then `asset --shot S --file out/x.mp4 --kind movie --quote "…"`. Bind only what the shot's subjects and place need, and say why each reference is bound.
`vw visuals record --gaps all --quote "<their yes>"` records every gap whose shots are done; repeat as the rest finish. `vw next` moves on when all gaps are recorded.

Brand: the brief's client card carries the palette, the brand guidelines and the competitors; generated pictures follow the palette and guidelines, never show a competitor, and never generate a logo. A real logo for a reference element: `vw brand fetch` saves the directory's logo files under in/brand/, then `vw visuals supply --element E --file in/brand/<name>`.

stages.name: assembly
steps: `vw assembly prepare`: it lists every gap fill on one line (slot frames, what the take or asset covers, the default: trim from frame 0, or hold the last frame when the take is short; issues such as untagged colour or rotation) and the shots the logs flagged as shaky.

Show the operator that table and ask once: any fill to change (start offset, trim or hold), any flagged shot to stabilise with FFmpeg (counted in the zoom cap), and for each fill with an issue whether to use it as it is or swap it in visuals. Record only the exceptions: `vw assembly choose --shot S --offset f --end trim|hold_last [--accept-as-is]`, or several in out/fills.json with `--file out/fills.json`; `vw assembly stabilize --sub X --choice ffmpeg`. The defaults need no command.

`vw assembly build`, `vw assembly render` (A1 narration with one measured gain, A2 nat sound at the blueprint band, a -3 dBTP ceiling on the mix, no music), `vw assembly status --wait 900` until the film is ready, `vw assembly fetch` (it prints the loudness against the targets). The operator watches AND listens.

On their yes (it must say watched and listened): `vw assembly record --quote "<their words>"` records the review and the output together. On changes: `vw assembly review --decision changes --notes "…" [--frame-note mm:ss:note] --quote "…"`, change the choices the notes name, build and render again (only the changed fills are re-encoded). On a no: `--decision rejected` and `vw revise --stage visuals` or `--stage master` as the notes say.

stages.name: delivery
steps: `vw delivery bundle` writes the package manifest (approved film, narration, originals used, normalised fills, plans, SRT, finishing checklist, media-pool CSV, OPEN-EDIT).

On the operator's computer (Windows or Mac): `vw pull <code>`, then `vw delivery check` (is Resolve installed, Studio or free, which version, enough disk; the download does not start without it), `vw delivery download` (the whole edit into runs/<code>/edit/, three files at a time, then counted and cross-checked: every file's size and fingerprint, the voiceover byte-identical, every cut pointing at a present file, the timeline's length and cut count equal to the film; the timeline is then written with this computer's paths), `vw delivery open` (free Resolve: three steps, File > Import > Timeline, then the operator plays the start, the middle and the end next to Approved-film.mp4; on their yes `vw delivery confirm --quote "<their words>"`; Resolve Studio, running with external scripting on: `vw delivery open` imports the timeline, exports .drp and .drt into Timeline/ and reads it back at 0 frames), then `vw delivery zip` for the editor. When the camera files are copies, before the handover: `vw delivery relink-check --originals "<folder>"` compares each original with Relink-list.csv and says per file: relinks as is, renamed (the relinked timeline points at the real name), a corrected timeline written (timecode), line up by hand (cuts listed with frame grabs), two originals fit (the operator picks), or no original found. `vw delivery resolve --run` is replaced; never run it (design/107).

Back on the build machine: ask the five questions (watched the film, listened, read the subtitles, the timeline matched the film, package complete) and `vw delivery final --quote "<their words>"`. Then `vw close` (retention: final film and package, narration, approved visuals, records; everything else deleted).
